risk_if_not_implemented: Without Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Protection, unauthorized individuals may gain physical access to facilities and equipment, enabling theft, tampering, damage or safety incidents. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss, Theft or Damage of Assets (R-AM-1), Physical / Environmental Damage (R-SF-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to natural threats NT-2, NT-3, NT-4, NT-5, NT-6, NT-8, NT-9, NT-10, NT-11, NT-12, NT-13, NT-14; Nuclear, Biological and Chemical (NBC) Weapons (MT-4), Technical / Mechanical Failure (MT-10), Product Defect / Design Failure (MT-23).

compensating_control_1.name: Supporting Utilities
compensating_control_1.description: Facility security mechanisms exist to protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction.
compensating_control_1.justification: Supporting Utilities (PES-20) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Protection (PES-31) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Facility applicability. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS)
compensating_control_2.description:
Mechanisms exist to operate a Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) to achieve resilient Technology Assets, Applications, Services and/or Data (TAASD) during:
(1) Routine operations; and
(2) Adverse conditions.
compensating_control_2.justification: Business Continuity Management System (BCMS) (BCD-02) provides resilience and recovery capability that compensates for the absence of Electromagnetic Pulse (EMP) Protection (PES-31) by ensuring the organization can restore operations and data when the primary control is absent. Given the facility and physical environment focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
